title: ServiceTitan MCP esbuild Upgrade
roughIdea: Resolve the remaining low-severity esbuild npm audit advisory safely after the lockfile-only audit repair left it parked.
targetUser: Maintainer of the public @rowvyn/servicetitan-mcp package and downstream MCP users who rely on stable Node 22 builds.
problem: npm audit still reports GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr for direct devDependency esbuild 0.27.x. npm marks the fix as semver-major because esbuild is pre-1.0 and recommends esbuild 0.28.1.
desiredOutcome: Upgrade esbuild to 0.28.1 and upgrade the Vitest/Vite test-toolchain path enough to remove the nested vulnerable esbuild, prove the Node 22 ESM build output and test suite still pass, publish through a PR only after checks are green, and avoid any npm release/deploy/live ServiceTitan API call.

in: Update direct devDependency esbuild from ^0.27.3 to ^0.28.1
Update Vitest tooling from v3 to v4 so the transitive Vite path can move to Vite 8, which no longer depends on esbuild
Run local install, audit, typecheck, lint, tests, build, docs generation, package dry-run, and diff checks
Open and merge a focused GitHub PR only if validation and CI pass
out: No unrelated dependency modernization beyond the Vitest/Vite path required to clear the esbuild advisory

constraints: Repo targets Node >=22 and CI runs Node 22.x.
Release workflow runs only on v* tags, so a normal PR merge should not publish.
esbuild is used by scripts/build.mjs through the JS build() API, not as production runtime code.
After the direct esbuild bump, npm audit still found vulnerable esbuild under node_modules/vite/node_modules/esbuild via Vitest 3.2.6.
Keep the existing package architecture and tool catalog intact.
preferredToolsRuntime: Existing scripts: build, typecheck, lint, test, docs:tools, prepublishOnly

risks.risk: esbuild pre-1.0 semver-major behavior change breaks bundling.
risks.mitigation: Run npm run build, inspect output, run package dry-run, and let GitHub CI repeat build/test on Node 22.x.

risks.risk: Vitest 4 behavior differs from Vitest 3 and changes test execution.
risks.mitigation: Run the full 273-test suite locally and in GitHub CI; inspect any failing test for real behavior change before adapting.
Run npm run docs:tools and require a clean git diff unless generated output is intentionally updated.
Do not push tags; verify release workflow is tag-only and npm latest remains 2.6.0 after merge.

assumptions: Trell's 'see that it is done safely' approves a focused PR/merge if local validation and CI are green.
A package release is not required because this is a devDependency-only build-tool change and package version stays 2.6.0.
